notes: Transcribed from SIR 2016-5118 ver. 1.2 (November 2017; the version history says ver. 1.2 revised Regression Regions 1 and 2 in Tables 6 and 7). Equations, n, Sp and ranges from Table 6 (report p. 36); model error variance and covariance [X^T Lambda^-1 X]^-1 from Table 7 (pp. 39-42). Table 6 and Table 7 were double-entered (hand transcription from rendered pages vs. a regex parse of pdftotext -table output): 804 cells, 0 disagreements. Every equation also reproduces the report's own Table 8 regional-regression estimates at the Table 5 gage characteristics (4,064 of 4,120 values exact at 3 significant figures, 46 more within 1%), and matches live NSS (Washington, citation 150, regression regions 717-720, codes GC1750-GC1753), whose equation strings carry the same coefficients. Equation forms: Regions 1 and 2 Q = a A^b 10^(cP) / 10^(d CAN); Region 3 Q = a A^b P^c; Region 4 Q = a A^b 10^(cP). Stored as intercept = log10(a), DRNAREA log10, PRECPRIS10 identity (log10 in Region 3), CANOPY_PCT identity with coefficient -d. PRECPRIS10 and CANOPY_PCT are NSS's codes for the report's P (PRISM 1981-2010 mean annual precipitation, Table 5 PRECIP) and CAN (NLCD 2001 area-weighted canopy, percent). Limits are Table 6's ranges; NSS's differ slightly (it rounds them: Region 1 DRNAREA max 3310 vs 3,304; Region 3 PRECPRIS10 min 33.2 vs 33.29). Units: model_error_variance is Table 7's sigma_delta^2 (log10 units squared) as printed. sep_log is Table 6's Sp (average standard error of prediction, percent) converted as sqrt(ln(1 + (Sp/100)^2)) / ln(10). The report publishes no AVP, so avp is not stored; SEM and pseudo-R2 are not stored. n_sites is Table 6's number of stations; with it evaluate() reproduces Table 7's t critical values (1.662, 1.6630, 1.6559, 1.656). Covariance: Regions 1 and 2 are taken at full precision from the report's Flood Q Tools workbook (sir20165118_floodqtools.xlsm, sheet 'Flood Q Regression Tool'), whose values round to Table 7's 4 significant figures except at three cells where Table 7 is misprinted: Region 1 AEP 0.01 (CAN, A) is printed +1.560e-5 below the diagonal but -1.560e-5 above it (workbook -1.5602854e-5); Region 2 AEP 0.5 (P, Intercept) is printed -1.276e-4 below the diagonal but -1.267e-4 above it (workbook -1.2665308e-4); Region 2 AEP 0.1 (P, P) is printed 5.287e-6 (workbook 5.2784385e-6). The workbook matrix reproduces the report's worked example (p. 43: Region 2, AEP 0.01, x'Ux = 0.00868359) exactly; Table 7's rounded values give 0.0086777. Region 3's covariance is Table 7 as printed (the workbook carries the same 4 significant figures). The row order is intercept then A, P, CAN, in the log10(A), raw P, raw CAN basis: MEV + mean x'Ux over each region's calibration gages (Table 5, 'Used in Regional Regression? = Yes') reproduces Sp^2 within 0.5% (Regions 1 and 2) and 1.1% (Region 3). Region 4 carries no covariance, and after checking every source the report offers it cannot be stored consistently. Table 7's Region 4 matrix (column header 'P (inches)', no footnote), applied with raw P, gives MEV + mean x'Ux over the 139 calibration gages of 0.31 to 0.45, 6.7 to 8.3 times Table 6's Sp^2, and its P variance (3.27e-5) would make the P coefficient (0.0073) insignificant (t about 1.3); with P/10 in place of P that check agrees within about 1% at every AEP. Nothing in the report documents P/10, however, and the report's own computations all use raw P: (1) the text (eq. 8) defines X_i as the basin characteristics 'as used in the regression equation'; (2) the Flood Q Tools workbook builds Region 4's row as [1, LOG10(DA), P] with P in inches (cell BN4 = $Q$11) against Table 7's printed matrix, and its VBA modules only format cells; (3) Table 8's weighted estimates come from WIE (report eq. 10), whose regression variance is MEV + x'Ux. From Table 8 alone, w = (log Qwtd - log Qreg) / (log Qsta - log Qreg) = Vr / (Vs + Vr) and the line-4 95-percent interval Vw = w Vs recover Vr = Vw / (1 - w) at each gage. Over 96 Region 4 gages (338 gage-AEP pairs with |log Qsta - log Qreg| >= 0.05 and 0.02 < w < 0.98) the median ratio of that Vr to MEV + x'Ux is 0.985 with raw P and 4.0 with P/10; the same inversion gives 1.000 to 1.002 for Regions 1 to 3 with the stored matrices (one Region 4 gage, 14226800, is an outlier at 0.13). So the P/10 reading is contradicted by the report's own Table 8, and the printed matrix with raw P is contradicted by its Table 6 Sp. Neither basis is stored; Region 4 intervals fall back to sep_log. The Flood Q Tools workbook's own Region 2 DRNAREA range (0.42-1820) disagrees with Table 6 (0.42-1,322) and with NSS (1330); Table 6 is used. The workbook also gives a to more digits than Table 6 at three AEPs (Region 2 AEP 0.002 169.824; Region 4 AEP 0.005 108.893 and 0.002 134.276); Table 6's printed values, which NSS also uses, are stored. NSS labels its citation ver. 1.1 (October 2016) but its Region 1 and 2 coefficients are ver. 1.2's.
